topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Under C.R.S. 12-10-202, before a real estate broker's license can be granted, an applicant must establish compliance with which combination of requirements?
choice_a: Education, experience, and testing; truthfulness, honesty, and good moral character; and competency to safeguard the public interest
choice_b: Only payment of the licensing fee and completion of a background check
choice_c: Membership in good standing with a local real estate board
choice_d: Ownership of a registered brokerage office
explanation: 12-10-202 states no license shall be granted until the person establishes compliance with the provisions concerning education, experience, and testing; truthfulness and honesty and otherwise good moral character; and competency to transact business so as to safeguard the interest of the public.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: In determining an applicant's character under 12-10-202, which statute governs the commission's determination?
choice_a: Section 12-10-203
choice_b: Section 24-5-101
choice_c: Section 22-2-119.3
choice_d: Section 23-64
explanation: 12-10-202 states that in determining the person's character, the commission shall be governed by section 24-5-101.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per 12-10-203(1)(b)(I), when must an applicant submit fingerprints to the Colorado Bureau of Investigation?
choice_a: After receiving a conditional license
choice_b: Only if requested by the commission after review
choice_c: Prior to submitting the license application
choice_d: Within 90 days after the license is issued
explanation: 12-10-203(1)(b)(I) requires that prior to submitting an application for a license, each applicant shall submit a set of fingerprints to the Colorado Bureau of Investigation for a state and national fingerprint-based criminal history record check.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Under 12-10-203(2), what must a real estate broker licensed under Part 2 maintain within Colorado, subject to a stated statutory exception?
choice_a: A minimum of two full-time employees
choice_b: A dedicated trust account at a Colorado-chartered bank
choice_c: Errors and omissions insurance
choice_d: A place of business
explanation: 12-10-203(2) requires every real estate broker licensed under Part 2 to maintain a place of business within the state, except as provided in section 12-10-208.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: What is the minimum age required for an applicant for a broker's license under 12-10-203(4)(a)?
explanation: 12-10-203(4)(a) states an applicant for a broker's license shall be at least eighteen years of age.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per 12-10-203(4)(a), an applicant can satisfy the education prerequisite by furnishing proof of which of the following?
choice_a: Two years' experience assisting a licensed broker
choice_b: Either a degree from an accredited college/university with a major course of study in real estate, OR completion of commission-approved courses of study
choice_c: A high school diploma plus a background check
choice_d: Completion of the Employing Broker Refresher Course only
explanation: 12-10-203(4)(a) requires proof satisfactory to the commission that the applicant has either received a degree with a major course of study in real estate or has successfully completed commission-approved courses of study.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Under 12-10-203(4)(a)(I), how many hours of classroom instruction (or equivalent correspondent hours) in real estate law and real estate practice are required?
explanation: 12-10-203(4)(a)(I) requires forty-eight hours of classroom instruction or equivalent correspondent hours in real estate law and real estate practice.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Under 12-10-203(4)(a)(II), how many hours of instruction in understanding and preparation of Colorado real estate contracts are required?
explanation: 12-10-203(4)(a)(II) requires forty-eight hours of classroom instruction or equivalent correspondent hours in understanding and preparation of Colorado real estate contracts.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Under Rule 2.1.A.2, what is the minimum number of hours required in Trust Accounts and Record Keeping for the Associate Broker educational path?
explanation: Rule 2.1.A.2.d requires not less than eight hours of instruction in Trust Accounts and Record Keeping as part of the 168-hour Associate Broker course breakdown.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Under Rule 2.1.A.2, what is the minimum number of hours required in Practical Application for the Associate Broker educational path?
explanation: Rule 2.1.A.2.f requires not less than thirty-two hours of instruction in Practical Application, part of the total 168 hours required for an Associate Broker license.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per 12-10-203(4)(b), an applicant who has already been licensed as a real estate broker in another jurisdiction is required to complete only which course(s)?
choice_a: All four subject areas listed in 12-10-203(4)(a)
choice_b: Only the real estate law and practice course
choice_c: The Colorado real estate contracts course and the real estate closings portion of the 72-hour area of study
choice_d: No coursework, only the exam
explanation: 12-10-203(4)(b) requires an applicant already licensed as a broker elsewhere to complete only the course of study comprising subsections (4)(a)(II) (Colorado contracts) and (4)(a)(III)(B) (real estate closings).

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per Rule 2.1.B and 12-10-203(5)(c)(II), how many hours of instruction in Brokerage Administration must an Employing Broker level applicant complete?
explanation: Rule 2.1.B requires an applicant for an Employing Broker level license to complete twenty-four hours of classroom instruction or equivalent Distance Learning hours in Brokerage Administration.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per Rule 2.1.D, under what conditions may the Commission audit approved courses of study?
choice_a: Only once per year, with 30 days' notice and a fee
choice_b: At any time and at no cost
choice_c: Only if a student files a complaint
choice_d: Only during the first year a course is approved
explanation: Rule 2.1.D states the Commission may audit the approved courses of study at any time and at no cost, requesting instructional materials and attendance records to verify adherence to the approved course of study.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per Rule 2.2.A, the Real Estate Licensing Examination consists of which two parts?
choice_a: A written part and an oral part
choice_b: An ethics part and a mathematics part
choice_c: A national part and a Colorado part
choice_d: A closing statement part and a contracts part
explanation: Rule 2.2.A states the Real Estate Licensing Examination is administered by a third-party testing service and consists of two parts: a national part and a Colorado part.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per 12-10-203(5)(a), in addition to topics like ethics, appraisal, and financing, what specific task must the broker's licensing examination include?
choice_a: Drafting a listing contract from scratch
choice_b: An oral interview before the commission
choice_c: A property inspection report
choice_d: Preparation of a real estate closing statement
explanation: 12-10-203(5)(a) states the examination for a broker's license shall also include the preparation of a real estate closing statement.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per Rule 2.2.F, how long is a passing score on either part of the Real Estate Licensing Examination valid?
choice_a: 1 year
choice_b: 6 months
choice_c: 18 months
choice_d: 2 years
explanation: Rule 2.2.F states a passing score for either part of the exam is valid for one year, and failure to submit a complete application within that year invalidates the score.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per Rule 2.2.E, what may an applicant do if they fail one or both parts of the Real Estate Licensing Examination?
choice_a: Wait a mandatory two years before reapplying
choice_b: Retake the failed part(s) at a subsequent time
choice_c: Appeal directly to the Colorado Bureau of Investigation
choice_d: Automatically receive a temporary license
explanation: Rule 2.2.E states that if an applicant fails one or both parts of the exam, the applicant may retake the failed part(s) at a subsequent time.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per Rule 2.2.G, to whom will the Commission certify examination results?
choice_a: Any state or agency that requests them, regardless of licensure status
choice_b: Only the applicant's employing broker
choice_c: Only a person who is or has been licensed as a Broker
choice_d: No one, under any circumstances
explanation: Rule 2.2.G states the Commission will not certify examination results to any person, state, or agency concerning a person who has taken the exam unless that person is or has been licensed as a Broker.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per 12-10-203(5)(b), an applicant who has held a broker's license in another jurisdiction that administers a broker's exam, for two or more years, may be issued a Colorado broker's license if the applicant establishes what?
choice_a: They passed the Colorado exam with a perfect score
choice_b: They completed 168 hours of Colorado-specific coursework
choice_c: They are sponsored by a Colorado Employing Broker
choice_d: They possess credentials and qualifications substantively equivalent to Colorado's licensure-by-examination requirements
explanation: 12-10-203(5)(b) allows issuance of a broker's license to such an applicant if they establish that their credentials and qualifications are substantively equivalent to Colorado's licensure-by-examination requirements.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per Rule 2.3, under what circumstance may the Commission acquire a name-based criminal history record check instead of relying on fingerprints?
choice_a: For an applicant who has twice submitted to a fingerprint-based check and whose fingerprints are unclassifiable
choice_b: Whenever an applicant is over age 60
choice_c: For all out-of-state applicants automatically
choice_d: Whenever the applicant declines to be fingerprinted
explanation: Rule 2.3 states the Commission may acquire a name-based criminal history record check for an applicant who has twice submitted to a fingerprint-based check and whose fingerprints are unclassifiable.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per Rule 2.4, a certified license history from another jurisdiction submitted with an application must bear a date of not more than how many days prior to the submission date?
choice_a: 30 days
choice_b: 90 days
choice_c: 60 days
choice_d: 180 days
explanation: Rule 2.4 requires the certificate of licensing history to bear a date of not more than ninety days prior to the submission date of the application.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per Rule 2.5.A, what experience is prescribed for an applicant seeking a Colorado Associate Broker level license?
choice_a: One year working under a sponsoring broker
choice_b: Six months of transactional experience
choice_c: There are no prescribed experience requirements
choice_d: Two closed transactions
explanation: Rule 2.5.A states there are no prescribed experience requirements to apply for a Colorado Associate Broker level license.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per Rule 2.5.B, what must an applicant have held to qualify for an Independent Broker level license?
choice_a: An Employing Broker license for one year
choice_b: A real estate degree plus one closed transaction
choice_c: A broker's license in any state for six months
choice_d: An Associate Broker level license on Active status for at least two years preceding the application
explanation: Rule 2.5.B requires each applicant for an Independent Broker level license to have held an Associate Broker level license on Active status for at least two years preceding the date of application.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per Rule 2.5.C.3.a, an Employing Broker applicant applying on or after January 1, 2018 must accumulate at least how many points within the preceding five-year period?
choice_a: 50 points
choice_b: 25 points
choice_c: 75 points
choice_d: 100 points
explanation: Rule 2.5.C.3.a requires the applicant's evidence to qualify for a total of at least fifty points accumulated within the five-year period immediately preceding the date of application.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per Rule 2.5.C.3.a, how do points differ between a completed commercial sales transaction and a completed residential sales transaction?
choice_a: Both are worth 3 points
choice_b: A commercial sale is worth 6 points and a residential sale is worth 3 points
choice_c: A residential sale is worth 6 points and a commercial sale is worth 3 points
choice_d: Both are worth 6 points
explanation: Under the Employing Broker point system, each completed or closed commercial sales transaction is worth six points, while each completed or closed residential sales transaction is worth three points.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per 12-10-203(10), a licensed attorney applying for a broker's license must pass the examination after completing how many hours of classroom instruction, and in what subjects?
choice_a: 24 hours in Brokerage Administration
choice_b: 48 hours in real estate law and practice
choice_c: 12 hours in trust accounts, record keeping, and real estate closings
choice_d: 72 hours across all four core subject areas
explanation: 12-10-203(10) requires a licensed attorney to take and pass the examination after having completed twelve hours of classroom instruction or equivalent correspondent hours in trust accounts, record keeping, and real estate closings.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per 12-10-203(6)(b), before a license can be issued to a partnership, LLC, or corporation, what must the broker designated by that entity do?
choice_a: Post a surety bond in the entity's name
choice_b: Obtain a separate individual license first
choice_c: Wait two years after entity formation
choice_d: Submit to and pass the examination required by Part 2 on behalf of the entity
explanation: 12-10-203(6)(b) states no license shall be issued to a partnership, LLC, or corporation unless the broker designated by it submits to and passes the required examination on behalf of the entity.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per 12-10-203(6)(c), if a designated broker ceases to serve a partnership, LLC, or corporation, for how long may the director issue a temporary license to prevent hardship, with the possibility of one extension?
choice_a: Up to 90 days, with one extension of up to 90 additional days upon proper application and good cause
choice_b: Up to 30 days, non-extendable
choice_c: Up to 180 days, non-extendable
choice_d: Up to 60 days, with unlimited extensions
explanation: 12-10-203(6)(c) allows the director to issue a temporary license for a period not to exceed ninety days, extendable for one additional period not to exceed ninety days upon proper application and a showing of good cause.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per 12-10-203(7), who is personally responsible for the handling of earnest money deposits or escrow/trust funds received or disbursed by a partnership, LLC, or corporation?
choice_a: Only the entity itself, never an individual
choice_b: The broker designated to act as broker for the entity
choice_c: Every licensed broker employed by the entity equally
choice_d: The Colorado Real Estate Commission
explanation: 12-10-203(7) states the broker designated to act as broker for the entity is personally responsible for the handling of any earnest money deposits or escrow or trust funds received or disbursed by the entity.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per 12-10-203(8), a license for a broker registered as being in the employ of another broker shall not be issued under a fictitious or trade name, except for what circumstance?
choice_a: When the broker has a professional corporation
choice_b: When the broker uses a nickname commonly known in the community
choice_c: A married woman may elect to use her birth name
choice_d: When approved in writing by the employing broker
explanation: 12-10-203(8) prohibits issuing such a license under a fictitious or trade name, except that a married woman may elect to use her birth name.

topic: Licensing Requirements: Education, Experience, and Examination
question: Per Rule 2.10.C, how many Temporary Licenses (whether consecutive or not) may be issued to any corporation, partnership, or LLC during any eighteen-month period?
choice_a: Unlimited, as long as hardship is shown each time
choice_b: Only one, ever
choice_c: Three
choice_d: No more than two
explanation: Rule 2.10.C states no more than two Temporary Licenses may be issued to any corporation, partnership, or LLC, whether consecutive or not, during any eighteen-month period.
